audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Locke/Locke/Skill, but the prose sitting under them says the opposite: whys[0] 'Darius owns level 1', whys[1] 'Level 2 stays yours', whys[2] 'Level 3 is yours outright', whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 stay Darius-favored', whys[4] 'Level 6 is even'. The packet levelChart agrees with the prose (Darius x4, Skill, Locke, Skill).
audit.why: Locke has no ability that beats a melee bruiser before his ultimate: Ritual Nails is a 10/9/8/7/6s projectile, Soul Ignition costs him his own health for 18s at rank 1, and Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s that is simultaneously his engage and his only exit. Level 6 is where Purgatory genuinely evens it.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped to Darius for Levels 1 through 4-5, Skill at Level 6, Locke at First item, Skill at Two+ items — proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike was written as a clean trade ('the lane turns honest: your Guillotine reset game trades evenly with his Purgatory execute'), which misses what Purgatory actually does to your ultimate.
audit.why: Purgatory carries the grounding flag ('shuts off enemy dashes') and Riot's own text calls it a 'binding artifact' with a zone. Noxian Guillotine is a leap (dash flag on Darius R). If he lands Purgatory on you first, your R cannot carry you out of the zone — the execute race is not symmetric, it is decided by who throws first.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike, phases[4].why, whys[4] and content mid now state the binding-vs-leap interaction and tell you to fight before he throws, not after.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] (Itemization) says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.' That is the exact opposite of the truth, and it is the one item line a Darius player will act on.
audit.why: Soul Ignition (W) 'deal[s] damage to himself. At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect' — the refund is healing, so Grievous Wounds cuts it. The refund lands at the END of an 18/17/16/15/14s window, which makes the anti-heal TIMING, not the purchase, the decision. The _missing file lists this matchup under rule needs-antiheal for exactly this ability.
audit.corrected: Itemization line now tells you to buy Grievous Wounds and apply it before Soul Ignition expires; the first-item spike carries the same instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentions that Ashen Pursuit (E) is an auto-attack reset, and never gives Ritual Nails' real 950 range — instead it repeatedly frames Locke as a short-range champion you can simply out-range.
audit.why: Ritual Nails is 950 range, far outside Apprehend's 535. What actually brings him to you is that 'Locke can consume the marks to deal bonus damage with his attacks' — the marks only pay off on autos, so he has to walk into your pull range to cash them. Ashen Pursuit carries the autoReset flag, so his burst opens on an attack wind-up, not on a visible cast.
audit.corrected: tldr, phases[0].why and content early re-framed around 950-range poke that must be converted at auto range; that walk is the Apprehend window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. breakdown.cooldowns also asserts Ashen Pursuit 'resets on takedowns', which is nowhere in Riot's text.
audit.why: Verifiable numbers: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank, Ritual Nails 10s down to 6s, Soul Ignition 18s at rank 1, Purgatory 120/100/80s. The takedown-reset claim cannot be checked from the kit and has been removed rather than repeated.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the real numbers; the takedown-reset assertion dropped and logged in unverified.

audit.why: The packet's suspectName hit on spikes[0].text 'Crippling Strike's' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Crippling Strike is Darius' own W and the name is exact. Left untouched.

edits.after: Dodge the nails, force the brawl his 10s Ashen Pursuit can’t leave, and end fights above his execute floor. Grievous Wounds before Soul Ignition expires cuts the refund that keeps him alive.

edits.before: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Ritual Nails: 10s at rank 1, 6s at rank 5 — the marks are his whole engine; sidestep the recasts and his blink-in barely dents. - Ashen Pursuit: a flat 10s at every rank and his ONLY exit — the ten seconds after he spends it are the lane. - Soul Ignition: 18s at rank 1; anti-heal it before it expires. - Purgatory: 120s at rank 1 — never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.

edits.before: Locke wastes Ritual Nails — that is your full-commit window.
edits.after: Purgatory binds you in the zone; your R leap cannot carry you out.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Buy Grievous Wounds — it cuts the Soul Ignition refund.

edits.before: You own his effective range: he has to come close enough to poke that your Q outer-blade heal and E pull are always live. Level 2's W slow makes every exchange bleed your way, and 3 completes it — full Hemorrhage stacking plus the pull means one grab is a kill threat. Zone him, deny farm, and make him choose between CS and health.
edits.after: Ritual Nails outrange you at 950, but the marks only cash on his autos, so he has to step inside Apprehend to convert them. Level 2's W slow makes every exchange bleed your way, and 3 completes it — full Hemorrhage stacking plus the pull means one grab is a kill threat. Deny farm and make him choose between CS and health.

edits.before: At 6 the lane turns honest — your Guillotine reset game trades evenly with his Purgatory execute — and his first item is the stage to fear: AP scaling lets his R threshold and W burst convert any Darius he catches low. Reset before half HP, keep pulling him when your stacks are ready, and don't chase into fog.
edits.after: At 6 Purgatory binds you inside its zone, so Guillotine cannot leap you clear — and his first item is the stage to fear: AP scaling lets his R threshold and W burst convert any Darius he catches low. Commit in the ten seconds after Ashen Pursuit is spent, reset before half HP, and don't chase into fog.

edits.after: Purgatory binds you inside its zone, so your Guillotine cannot leap you clear — fight before he throws it, not after.

edits.before: His AP spike converts any Darius caught low — the one stage where you play respectful and stay topped up.
edits.after: His AP spike converts any Darius caught low — carry Grievous Wounds so Soul Ignition's refund cannot bail him out.

notes: Locke's R Purgatory carries the kit's grounding flag ('shuts off enemy dashes') and Riot calls it a 'binding artifact', which is why I wrote the binding-vs-Guillotine interaction — but Riot's description does not spell grounding out in words, so it is listed in unverified for a wiki check before this ships. Removed rather than repeated: breakdown.cooldowns claimed Ashen Pursuit 'resets on takedowns'; nothing in Riot's text supports that, so it is gone and logged. Not acted on: Soul Ignition carries a trueDamage flag, but Riot's text only describes damage Locke deals to HIMSELF, so the _missing file's 'resistances-invalidated' entry for this matchup looks like a flag misfire and no true-damage-to-you claim was written. Also not acted on: the repeated '125 range' framing for Locke appears in phases[0].why, breakdown.wave and report — the kit carries no basic-attack range, so I only corrected the places where I could substitute a verified number (Ritual Nails 950); breakdown.wave and the report's Wave Management line still say '125 range' and need a human call. The packet's suspectName on spikes[0].text is a false positive: 'Crippling Strike' is Darius' own W.
